summary: I downloaded and inspected every source end-to-end and built a working merge prototype. OpenJLPT is the Tanos/JLPT-Kanji.com word list (662/632/1784/1793/3463 = 8,334 vocab; 2,211 kanji) — good structure but with real defects: 889 entries have NO example sentences (563 of them N1), 27 readings contain garbage (POS markers like 「（感）」, slash-joined multi-readings, one true mojibake 「Uӣ[い」 for 賛成), 20 words are slash-joined multi-forms, and ~243 surface forms appear in two levels — many N3 rows are wrong-homophone EDICT lookups (はい → "wear/put on (sword)", どう → "child/servant"). The confirmed rule is: `reading` is empty exactly when the word is kana-only (0 kanji-containing words have an empty reading, across all 8,334), with 32 N3/N2 exceptions where the field was filled (sometimes with junk). Every gap is fixable at build time: JPDB v2.2 gives frequency ranks for 8,294/8,334 words, kanjium gives pitch accent for 8,194/8,334, kuromoji (npm, 4,521 sentences/sec) segments and reads every sentence, and jmdict-examples fills 656 of the 889 missing-example rows. My full merge produced 3.08 MB raw / 812 KB brotli for all five levels with readings repaired, frequency-sorted, pitch-annotated and pre-tokenized examples — N5 alone is 51 KB brotli. KanjiVG covers 2,211/2,211 JLPT kanji (457 KB brotli, rounded) and also carries component decomposition for free. A compact JMdict-common tap-a-word dictionary is 1.95 MB raw / 560 KB brotli; full JMdict sharded into 64 lazy shards has a largest shard of 195 KB gzip.

recommendations.title: Use OpenJLPT as the spine, but run a repair pass — do NOT ship it raw
recommendations.decision: Keep OpenJLPT's 8,334 rows as the canonical per-level vocab spine (it is the Tanos list, matches jlpt-vocab-api totals exactly for N5/N4/N1, and matches kanji-jouyou.json's jlpt_new distribution exactly for N5=79/N4=166/N3=367/N2=367). But at build time: (a) split the 20 slash-joined words into `word` + `alt[]`; (b) reject any `reading` that contains a non-kana char (27 rows) and refill from open-anki-jlpt-decks, then kuromoji; (c) drop the duplicate-across-level row where the lower-level entry already exists AND the higher-level meaning is a different homophone (the 243 collisions — quarantine, don't auto-merge).
recommendations.why: Verified by running the checks: 27 bad readings incl. genuine mojibake (N3 賛成 reading="Uӣ[い"), 12 rows whose reading is a POS marker 「（感）」「（副）」, and N3 rows whose meaning belongs to a homophone (そこ→"bottom/sole"=底, はい→"wear/put on (sword)"=佩く, どう→"child/servant/foolishness"=童). My repair pass fixed 19 readings automatically and left N5 with 0 missing readings.

recommendations.title: Sort every level by JPDB frequency rank, not alphabetically
recommendations.decision: Bake `f` (JPDB v2.2 rank) onto every word and ship each level pre-sorted ascending by rank. Expose a 'Most useful first' vs 'A–Z' toggle. Word #1 in N5 becomes する (rank 11), ある (14) — exactly the fast-start order the user asked for.
recommendations.why: JPDB covers 8,294/8,334 (99.5%) of JLPT vocab. Measured medians: N5=1625, N4=2276, N3=3074, N2=12724, N1=12325. OpenJLPT's native order is alphabetical-by-kana, which buries する and ある deep in the list. Costs nothing at runtime since the sort happens at build time.

recommendations.title: Warn the builder: N2 and N1 are NOT frequency-ordered relative to each other
recommendations.decision: Do not present N2→N1 as 'harder = rarer'. Median JPDB rank is N2=12724 vs N1=12325 — N1 words are on average slightly MORE common than N2 words. For the 'basic fast → professional' arc, drive progression off frequency rank (a cross-level 'Top 1000 / Top 2000 / Top 5000' track) rather than off JLPT level alone.
recommendations.why: Measured directly from the JPDB rank join. Also 574/7141 (8%) of words that appear in both OpenJLPT and open-anki-jlpt-decks are assigned DIFFERENT levels (うるさい: OpenJLPT N3 vs Anki N5; 掛ける: N4 vs N5; パート: N4 vs N1). Level boundaries past N3 are genuinely fuzzy, so a frequency spine is more honest and more useful.

recommendations.title: Tokenize ALL Japanese text at build time with kuromoji — this is what makes tap-a-word work
recommendations.decision: npm install kuromoji. At build time tokenize every example sentence and every YouTube subtitle cue into `[surface, lemma|0, katakanaReading|0]` triples and bake them into the JSON. The app then renders each token as a tappable <span>, converts the katakana reading to hiragana for furigana, and looks up `lemma` in the JMdict index. Zero runtime tokenizer, zero MeCab, zero CORS.
recommendations.why: Verified working: kuromoji tokenized 今日は会議があるので、早めに会社へ行きます。 into 14 tokens with correct lemma (行き→行く) and reading (会議→カイギ). Benchmarked 14,362 sentences / 111,238 tokens in 3.18s (4,521 sent/s) after a 3.9s dict load. Token data for all examples adds only 246 KB brotli. Without this, tap-a-word on subtitles degrades to naive longest-match and will mis-split conjugated verbs.

recommendations.title: Ship jmdict-eng-common as the offline tap-a-word dictionary; lazy-load full JMdict in 64 shards
recommendations.decision: Bundle the compacted jmdict-eng-common (22,640 entries) as a single 560 KB brotli file loaded on first dictionary tap and cached by the service worker. For rare words, lazy-fetch one of 64 shards of the full 218,776-entry JMdict keyed by `firstCodePoint % 64`. Shard on demand, cache forever (JMdict is versioned by release tag).
recommendations.why: Measured: compact common = 1.95 MB raw / 770 KB gzip / 560 KB brotli, plus a 38,899-key surface→index map at 250 KB gzip. Full JMdict compact = 16.31 MB raw / 4.81 MB brotli; sharded x64 the largest single shard is only 195 KB gzip. A phone can hold the common dict in memory permanently and fetch a 195 KB shard in well under a second.

recommendations.title: Bundle KanjiVG stroke order — it is small and it covers 100% of JLPT kanji
recommendations.decision: Extract just the `d="..."` path strings from kanjivg-20250816.xml, round coordinates to 1 decimal, and ship as {kanji: [path,...]}. Animate with stroke-dasharray/stroke-dashoffset. Ship N5+N4 (245 kanji, 65 KB gzip) in the app shell and the rest (1,966 kanji) as a lazy 457 KB brotli file.
recommendations.why: Verified 2,211/2,211 JLPT kanji present in KanjiVG r20250816. Paths-only = 1.90 MB raw / 648 KB brotli; rounding to 1dp drops it to 1.59 MB raw / 457 KB brotli with no visible quality loss at phone sizes.

recommendations.title: Get radicals/components from the SAME KanjiVG file — skip kradfile
recommendations.decision: Parse `kvg:element="X"` and `kvg:radical="general"` attributes out of kanjivg.xml while extracting the paths. Produces {kanji: {c:[components], r:radical}} at 83 KB raw / 21 KB gzip covering 2,211/2,211 kanji (2,146 with sub-components, 1,841 with a marked radical). Build the reverse map (875 distinct components → kanji) for a radical-search screen.
recommendations.why: Measured. 語 → {c:[言,口,吾,五,二], r:言}; 曜 → {c:[日,翟,羽,隹,亻], r:日}. This is a richer, hierarchical decomposition than kradfile (which gives a flat unordered bag) and it comes from a file you are already downloading. kradfile (447 KB) and radkfile (340 KB) are still worth adding only if you want the classic 253-radical lookup grid.

recommendations.title: Word audio: JapanesePod101 CDN, with placeholder detection at build time
recommendations.decision: Use https://assets.languagepod101.com/dictionary/japanese/audiomp3.php?kanji=<enc>&kana=<enc>. At BUILD time, fetch each of the 8,334 words once and record a boolean `hasAudio`; treat any response of exactly 52,288 bytes (md5 7e2c2f954ef6…) as 'no recording' and hide the play button. Store the boolean in the vocab JSON; stream the mp3 from the CDN at runtime (with a service-worker cache-on-play). Do NOT bundle the mp3s.
recommendations.why: Verified: 日本語/にほんご → 200, audio/mpeg, 2,448 B; 猫/ねこ → 1,872 B; 食べる/たべる → 2,760 B; 企業戦士/きぎょうせんし → 8,208 B. Three different nonsense inputs (ぴゃぴゃぴゃ, ずずずずず, ほげほげほげ) ALL returned the identical 52,288-byte file md5 7e2c2f954ef6, confirming the placeholder. Note this CDN is not formally licensed for redistribution — link, don't rehost, and have a TTS fallback (SpeechSynthesis with a ja-JP voice) so the app still works offline.

recommendations.title: Sentence audio: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR, actually downloadable
recommendations.decision: For example sentences, prefer Tatoeba sentences that have audio. Query https://tatoeba.org/en/api_v0/search?from=jpn&to=eng&query=<word>&limit=10&has_audio=yes at build time, then fetch https://tatoeba.org/en/audio/download/<audioId>. Bundle a small curated set (e.g. 2 sentences × the top 1,000 words) and link the rest.
recommendations.why: Verified: search returned 200 with audios:[{id:221406, author:"yomi", download_url:"/en/audio/download/221406"}]; fetching that URL returned 200, audio/mpeg, 12,614 bytes, valid MPEG layer III 48kbps. License field on results reads "CC BY 2.0 FR" — redistributable with attribution, unlike the jpod101 CDN.

recommendations.title: Pitch accent from kanjium (CC BY-SA 4.0), baked in — no extra file
recommendations.decision: Parse the 124,137-line TSV (word \t reading \t comma-separated accent positions) and attach a `p` field to each vocab row. Lookup order: exact word+reading, then word alone, then reading alone. Render as the standard overline/downstep bar over the kana. 17,212 entries carry multiple valid accents — show the first and mark the word as having variants.
recommendations.why: Verified: 3,226,405 bytes, 200 OK, 124,134 unique word|reading keys. Coverage of JLPT vocab with the reading fallback = 8,194/8,334 (98.3%): N5 651/662, N4 613/632, N3 1756/1784, N2 1758/1793, N1 3416/3463. Baking it in costs ~0 extra bytes; the standalone JLPT-only map would be 67 KB gzip and the full map 730 KB brotli. License is explicitly CC BY-SA 4.0 in the README (the GitHub API reports NOASSERTION because there is no LICENSE file at the root — the README is authoritative).

recommendations.title: Fill the 889 missing example sentences from jmdict-examples-eng
recommendations.decision: Download jmdict-examples-eng (14.1 MB zip → 129.3 MB JSON), index its 32,306 Tatoeba-linked examples by every kanji and kana surface form (72,340 surfaces), and backfill OpenJLPT rows that have no examples. This is a build-time-only 129 MB file — never ships.
recommendations.why: Measured: 889 OpenJLPT rows have no `examples` key at all (N5 21, N4 32, N3 17, N2 256, N1 563). jmdict-examples can supply a sentence for 656 of them (N5 19/21, N4 28/32, N3 15/17, N2 199/256, N1 395/563). The remaining 233 are mostly N1 rare nouns — flag them in the UI as 'no example yet' rather than showing an empty card.

recommendations.title: Keep OpenJLPT's own example sentences as the PRIMARY ones — they are unusually beginner-friendly
recommendations.decision: Do not replace OpenJLPT examples with Tatoeba ones wholesale. Use OpenJLPT first, Tatoeba only as backfill.
recommendations.why: Measured: 14,362 examples, 12,196 unique, 0 empty ja, 0 empty en, 0 ja===en, and 7,445/7,445 first-examples actually CONTAIN the headword (100% — I checked). Median length is 11 characters, p90 = 19. Tatoeba sentences are much longer and harder. Only 2,276/12,196 (19%) of OpenJLPT sentences appear in Tatoeba, so they are a genuinely distinct, short, level-appropriate corpus. Minor caveat: a few sentences are reused across up to 7 different words (その内訳は？ appears 7 times).

recommendations.title: Cross-validate kanji levels with davidluzgouveia/kanji-data, and get WaniKani-style radical names from it
recommendations.decision: Fetch kanji-jouyou.json (984,796 bytes, 2,136 jouyou kanji). Use it to (a) confirm OpenJLPT kanji level assignments and (b) pull `wk_level`, `wk_meanings` and `wk_radicals` (English radical names like 'Sun') for friendlier kanji cards. Treat it as supplementary only.
recommendations.why: Verified 200 OK. Its jlpt_new distribution is {5:79, 4:166, 3:367, 2:367, 1:985} — identical to OpenJLPT for N5–N2, confirming both derive from Tanos. OpenJLPT's N1 has 1,232 because it includes 247 non-jouyou kanji. RISK: the GitHub API reports no license for this repo and the wk_* fields are WaniKani-derived, so the radical NAMES may be proprietary. Use the readings/levels freely; treat wk_meanings/wk_radicals as attribution-required-and-possibly-unsafe.

recommendations.title: Build kanji→vocab cross-links from JMdict-common, not from the JLPT list
recommendations.decision: For each of the 2,211 kanji, store up to 8 JMdict-common entry indices whose common kanji form contains it. Show them on the kanji detail page as 'words that use this kanji', with a badge if the word is in the user's current JLPT level.
recommendations.why: Measured both options. Using only OpenJLPT vocab covers 1,768/2,211 kanji (median 4 words each) at 32 KB gzip. Using jmdict-common covers 2,017/2,211 (median 9 words each) and capped at 8 per kanji costs only 37 KB gzip. JMdict-common is strictly better for 37 KB.

recommendations.title: Add kanjialive ka_data.csv for radical names, positions and example compounds
recommendations.decision: Fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanjialive/kanji-data-media/master/language-data/ka_data.csv (765,727 bytes, CC BY 4.0). It gives per-kanji: radical char, radical name in Japanese AND romaji, radical MEANING in English, radical position (left/top/enclosing), plus 5–9 curated example compounds with readings and glosses.
recommendations.why: Verified 200 OK and inspected the header. Row for 一 includes rad_name_ja=いち, rad_meaning="one, horizontal stroke", and 9 example compounds like 一年生（いちねんせい）/first-year student. This is the single best openly-licensed source of human-readable radical explanations — kradfile only gives you bare characters. Covers ~1,235 kanji (roughly N5–N3), which is exactly the range where beginners need it. Their media CDN path https://media.kanjialive.com/kanji_audio/ichi.mp3 returned 404, so do NOT rely on their audio without finding the correct pattern.

recommendations.title: Skip the Leeds/hingston frequency list and Forvo
recommendations.decision: Do not use hingston/japanese or the Forvo API.
recommendations.why: hingston's 15000-japanese-words.txt (127,231 bytes, 200 OK, CC BY 2.5) is a bare newline-separated word list with NO counts, derived from a 2000s-era web-crawl corpus — its top entries are particles (の, に, は, て, を) and it is strictly worse than JPDB, which is rank-based, covers 278,946 entries, and hits 99.5% of the JLPT list. Forvo's apifree endpoint returned HTTP 400 with the DEMO key; it requires a paid key and forbids caching, which breaks offline-first.

verified_facts.claim: All 5 OpenJLPT vocab JSONs download cleanly
verified_facts.evidence: HTTP 200 for all: vocab-n5 222,308 B / n4 218,895 B / n3 679,580 B / n2 680,482 B / n1 1,311,444 B. Item counts N5=662, N4=632, N3=1784, N2=1793, N1=3463, total 8,334 — exactly matching the orchestrator's figure.

verified_facts.claim: All 5 OpenJLPT kanji JSONs download cleanly; total 2,211 with zero duplicates across levels
verified_facts.evidence: HTTP 200: kanji-n5 22,701 B / n4 49,031 B / n3 117,134 B / n2 105,985 B / n1 343,931 B. Counts 79/166/367/367/1232 = 2,211. 2,211 unique characters, 0 appearing in more than one level, 0 non-CJK or multi-char entries.

verified_facts.claim: OpenJLPT vocab field completeness: word/reading/meanings/level present on all 8,334; examples missing on 889
verified_facts.evidence: Field presence counts: word 8334, reading 8334, meanings 8334, level 8334, examples 7445. Rows with no `examples` key: N5=21, N4=32, N3=17, N2=256, N1=563 (total 889). Zero rows have an empty `examples` array. Zero rows have empty meanings.

verified_facts.claim: Example-count breakdown per level
verified_facts.evidence: 0 examples / 1 example / 2+ examples: N5 21/6/635, N4 32/6/594, N3 17/6/1761, N2 256/162/1375, N1 563/348/2552. Total 14,362 example sentences, 12,196 unique Japanese sentences.

verified_facts.claim: CONFIRMED: OpenJLPT leaves `reading` empty exactly for kana-only words
verified_facts.evidence: Across all 8,334 rows, the count of words CONTAINING kanji with an empty reading is exactly 0. 1,096 rows have an empty reading and every one of them is kana-only. Empty-reading counts per level: N5=163, N4=141, N3=217, N2=295, N1=280. The converse has 32 exceptions: 32 kana-only words DO have a filled reading (all in N3/N2, e.g. いえ→いえ, but also うん→「（感）」).

verified_facts.claim: 27 reading fields contain non-kana characters, including one genuine mojibake
verified_facts.evidence: Examples found: N3 賛成 reading="Uӣ[い" (mojibake); N3 うん/しまった/すみません/ね/はい/よろしく reading="（感）"; N3 ふと reading="（副）"; N2 だいいち reading="（副）"; N3 とん reading="（1000" (truncated); N5 何 reading="なん/なに"; N5 十 reading="じゅう とお" (space-separated); N2 じゅうたん reading="（カーペット）".

verified_facts.claim: 20 OpenJLPT words are slash-joined multi-forms that must be split
verified_facts.evidence: e.g. N5 「いい/よい」, 「キロ/キログラム」, 「ラジカセ / ラジオカセット」 (with spaces), 「伯父/叔父」[おじいさん], N4 「けれど/けれども」, 「コンピュータ/コンピューター」, 「やはり/やっぱり」, 「レポート/リポート」. Note 「伯父/叔父」 has the WRONG reading attached (おじいさん = grandfather, not おじ = uncle).

verified_facts.claim: 243 surface forms appear in more than one JLPT level, and many N3 entries are wrong-homophone EDICT lookups
verified_facts.evidence: Only 1 exact word|reading duplicate (けれど/けれども in N4 and N2). But 243 words share a surface across levels with different readings/meanings. Clear errors: そこ N5="that place" vs N3[そこ]="bottom/sole" (=底); はい N5="yes" vs N3[（感）]="wear/put on (sword)" (=佩く); どう N5="how" vs N3[（接。副）]="child/servant/foolishness" (=童); ね N3[（感）]="value/price/cost" (=値). Legitimate ones also exist: 悪い N5[わるい] vs N1[にくい], 一昨日 N5[おととい] vs N2[いっさくじつ].

verified_facts.claim: No mojibake or Latin characters in any OpenJLPT headword
verified_facts.evidence: Scan for U+FFFD or [A-Za-z] in the `word` field across all 8,334 rows returned 0 hits. (The one mojibake is in a `reading` field, not a `word`.)

verified_facts.claim: Every OpenJLPT first example sentence actually contains its headword
verified_facts.evidence: 7,445/7,445 checked — 0 failures. Sentences are short: median 11 chars, p90 19, max 60. A handful are reused across words: 「その内訳は？」 appears 7 times, 「大学生です。」/「先生が来る。」/「土曜日だよ。」/「工業都市です。」 6 times each.

verified_facts.claim: jlpt-vocab-api works, paginates via offset, and reports totals that nearly match OpenJLPT
verified_facts.evidence: HTTP 200. Response shape {total, offset, limit, words:[{word, meaning, furigana, romaji, level}]}. Totals: N5=662, N4=632, N3=1797, N2=1831, N1=3463 (vs OpenJLPT 662/632/1784/1793/3463 — N3 differs by 13, N2 by 38). offset=100&limit=3 returned the correct 3 rows; offset=660&limit=5 on a 662-row set returned [] (off-by-something bug at the tail). Adds romaji, which OpenJLPT lacks.

verified_facts.claim: open-anki-jlpt-decks CSVs download and disagree with OpenJLPT on 8% of shared words
verified_facts.evidence: HTTP 200: n1 191,444 B / n2 135,869 B / n3 167,423 B / n4 49,627 B / n5 63,965 B. Parsed rows: N5=718, N4=668, N3=2140, N2=1906, N1=2699 (8,131 rows, 7,896 unique expressions). Overlap with OpenJLPT = 7,141 words; level AGREE 6,567 (92.0%), DISAGREE 574 (8.0%); OpenJLPT-only 948, Anki-only 755. Disagreement examples: うるさい OpenJLPT N3 / Anki N5; 掛ける N4 / N5; パート N4 / N1; スリッパ N5 / N2; お腹 N3 / N5.

verified_facts.claim: open-anki-jlpt-decks can fill 921 of OpenJLPT's 1,096 empty readings
verified_facts.evidence: Of the 1,096 OpenJLPT rows with an empty `reading`, 921 have a matching expression in the Anki CSVs with a non-empty reading column. (These are all kana-only words where the reading equals the word, so this is a low-value fix — the real use is repairing the 27 corrupt readings.)

verified_facts.claim: jmdict-simplified latest release is 3.6.2+20260914172325 with 32 assets
verified_facts.evidence: GitHub API 200. Key asset sizes: jmdict-eng-common .zip 1.38 MB, jmdict-eng .zip 10.99 MB, jmdict-examples-eng .zip 13.49 MB, kanjidic2-en .zip 1.20 MB, kradfile .zip 0.10 MB, radkfile .zip 0.13 MB. Download URLs must percent-encode the '+' in the TAG path segment (%2B) but NOT in the filename.

verified_facts.claim: jmdict-eng-common: 22,640 entries, 16,507,660 bytes uncompressed
verified_facts.evidence: Downloaded 1,442,079 B zip (HTTP 200), unzipped to 16.5 MB. Top-level keys: version, languages, commonOnly, dictDate, dictRevisions, tags (266 tags), words. Entry shape {id, kanji[{common,text,tags}], kana[{common,text,tags,appliesToKanji}], sense[{partOfSpeech, appliesToKanji, appliesToKana, related, antonym, field, dialect, misc, info, languageSource, gloss[{lang,gender,type,text}]}]}. Totals: 26,556 kanji forms (18,211 marked common), 27,598 kana forms, 37,143 senses, 87,488 glosses.

verified_facts.evidence: Built [id, kanjiForms.join('|'), kanaForms.join('|'), [[pos, glosses.join('; '), misc?]]] capped at 3 senses / 4 glosses / 3 forms. 22,640 entries. Surface→index map: 38,899 keys, 0.53 MB raw / 250 KB gzip. Sharded by firstCodePoint%64: 64 shards, 2.22 MB raw total, 0.83 MB gzip total, largest shard 25 KB gzip.

verified_facts.claim: Full jmdict-eng is 117,917,570 bytes uncompressed; compacts to 16.31 MB raw / 4.81 MB brotli with 218,776 entries
verified_facts.evidence: Downloaded 11,519,548 B zip (HTTP 200). Same compaction: 218,776 entries, 16.31 MB raw / 7.05 MB gzip / 4.81 MB brotli. Surface index: 369,345 keys, 6.01 MB raw / 3.03 MB gzip. Sharded x64: 20.06 MB raw total, 7.17 MB gzip total, LARGEST SHARD 195 KB gzip — i.e. any single rare-word lookup needs at most a 195 KB fetch.

verified_facts.claim: jmdict-examples-eng contains 32,306 Tatoeba-linked example sentences and can fill 656 of the 889 missing-example rows
verified_facts.evidence: Downloaded 14,142,645 B zip (HTTP 200), unzipped to 129,287,388 B. 218,776 entries, 31,748 senses carry examples, 32,306 examples total. Example shape {source:{type:'tatoeba',value:id}, text:'<the headword form>', sentences:[{lang:'jpn',text},{lang:'eng',text}]}. Indexed by all surface forms → 72,340 keys. Backfill rate for OpenJLPT's example-less rows: N5 19/21, N4 28/32, N3 15/17, N2 199/256, N1 395/563 = 656/889.

verified_facts.claim: kanjidic2-en downloads: 14,830,710 B uncompressed, 10,384 characters, includes a jlptLevel field (OLD 4-level scale)
verified_facts.evidence: HTTP 200, 1,253,440 B zip. Shape {version, languages, dictDate, fileVersion, databaseVersion, characters[{literal, codepoints, radicals, misc:{grade, strokeCounts, variants, frequency, radicalNames, jlptLevel}, dictionaryReferences[...30+ incl. heisig/henshall/nelson], queryCodes, readingMeaning}]}. NOTE misc.jlptLevel for 日 is 4 — that is the OLD pre-2010 4-level scale, NOT N4. Do not use it for level assignment.

verified_facts.claim: kradfile and radkfile download and parse
verified_facts.evidence: HTTP 200: kradfile zip 106,080 B → 447,522 B JSON with 12,156 kanji, shape {kanji:{'亜':['｜','一','口']}}. radkfile zip 134,219 B → 339,960 B JSON with 253 radicals, shape {radicals:{'一':{strokeCount:1, code:null, kanji:[...]}}}.

verified_facts.claim: JPDB v2.2 frequency list downloads and covers 99.5% of JLPT vocab
verified_facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kuuuube/yomitan-dictionaries/main/dictionaries/JPDB_v2.2_Frequency_2024-10-13.zip → HTTP 200, 5,220,344 B. Contains index.json (frequencyMode:'rank-based', title 'JPDBv2') + term_meta_bank_1.json at 24,824,253 B with 278,946 rows, 274,218 unique surface keys. Row shape is ['の','freq',{value:1,displayValue:'1'}] with a second variant {reading, frequency:{value}}. JLPT coverage 8,294/8,334: N5 656/662, N4 625/632, N3 1779/1784, N2 1781/1793, N1 3453/3463. risks: OpenJLPT's N3 list contains wrong-homophone EDICT lookups. Shipping it raw will teach the user that はい means 'wear/put on (sword)' and そこ means 'bottom/sole'. You MUST run the quarantine list in code_or_data section 6. This is the single highest-severity data defect I found.

The `reading` field of 27 rows is not a reading at all — it is a part-of-speech marker like 「（感）」, a slash-joined pair, or in one case (N3 賛成) literal mojibake "Uӣ[い". If you feed these into a furigana renderer or a TTS call you will render garbage over the kanji. Validate every reading against /^[぀-ゟ゠-ヿーー・]+$/ before use.

The JLPT vocabulary lists are UNOFFICIAL. JEES has not published an official word list since 2010. OpenJLPT, open-anki-jlpt-decks and jlpt-vocab-api all trace back to Jonathan Waller's tanos.co.uk reconstruction (kanjium's README states this explicitly). They disagree with each other on 8% of shared words. Do not present levels as authoritative — say 'commonly-used JLPT study list' in the UI.

kanjidic2's misc.jlptLevel uses the OLD pre-2010 four-level scale (日 is 'jlptLevel: 4', meaning old level 4 = roughly today's N5). Using it as an N-level will invert your entire curriculum. Use OpenJLPT's level or kanji-jouyou.json's jlpt_new instead.

The JapanesePod101 CDN returns HTTP 200 with a 52,288-byte 'no recording' placeholder rather than a 404. If you don't check the byte length you will render a play button on thousands of words that plays a stock message. Also: that CDN has no public license for redistribution, it can be rate-limited or pulled at any time, and it requires a network connection — so an offline-first app needs a SpeechSynthesis ja-JP fallback, not just a dead button.

davidluzgouveia/kanji-data has NO license file (GitHub API returns null) and its wk_level / wk_meanings / wk_radicals fields are derived from WaniKani, whose content is proprietary. Use it for level cross-validation only; do not ship the WaniKani radical names or mnemonic-style keywords.

Kanji Alive's media CDN is not where you'd guess — https://media.kanjialive.com/kanji_audio/ichi.mp3 returned 404 text/html, and their language-data/radicals.csv is also 404. Only ka_data.csv (765,727 B) is confirmed. Don't design a feature around their audio without verifying the real path first.

889 OpenJLPT words have no example sentence and 233 of them cannot be filled from jmdict-examples (almost all N1). A flashcard UI that assumes an example exists will render an empty card. Handle the null case explicitly.

Several OpenJLPT example sentences are reused across up to 7 different headwords (「その内訳は？」 appears 7 times). If your flashcard algorithm shows the example on the front, the user will see the same sentence repeatedly and can pattern-match the answer. De-duplicate or show the example only on the back.

kuromoji's dictionary is ~15 MB of .dat.gz files. It is a BUILD-TIME dependency only — never bundle it into the PWA. If anyone is tempted to tokenize in the browser, that decision alone blows the entire data budget seven times over.

EDRDG data (JMdict, KANJIDIC, KRADFILE) is CC-BY-SA, and kanjium and OpenJLPT are CC-BY-SA 4.0. ShareAlike is viral over the derived data files. You can keep the app CODE under any license, but the shipped data/*.json files must carry a CC-BY-SA notice and an attribution page naming EDRDG/Jim Breen, OpenJLPT, kanjium (with Uros O.'s exact required sentence, which is quoted in the kanjium README), KanjiVG, Tatoeba and Kanji Alive.

The jmdict-simplified release TAG contains a literal '+' that must be percent-encoded as %2B in the URL path segment, while the FILENAME segment must keep the raw '+'. Getting this backwards yields a 404. The tag also changes on every release, so pin 3.6.2+20260914172325 in the build script rather than resolving 'latest' at build time.

jlpt-vocab-api's offset parameter misbehaves at the tail: offset=660&limit=5 on a 662-row set returned an empty array. If you use it as a gap-filler, page from the start rather than seeking near the end.

JPDB frequency ranks come from an anime/light-novel/visual-novel corpus. They are excellent for 'useful in real Japanese' but they are NOT business-Japanese frequencies. For the user's professional/workplace goal, JPDB will under-rank 弊社, 御中, 恐れ入りますが and similar keigo. Plan a separate hand-curated business track rather than assuming frequency ordering covers it.

OpenJLPT grammar is only ~20 points per level (9-10 KB per file). That is roughly a quarter of what a real JLPT level needs. This is outside my scope but it is the weakest link in the whole data set — whoever owns grammar must source it elsewhere.
